summary: Concrete observation tower on the TN-NC line, now called Kuwohi Observation Tower; built 1959 by the NPS with a fire cab that was dropped; NRHP-listed 2012; reached on foot.

facts.design: Reinforced concrete observation tower by Bebb and Olson, 45 ft tall, with a 375 ft spiral ramp to the platform; an enclosed fire lookout cab planned in early designs was removed
facts.agency: National Park Service, Great Smoky Mountains National Park

access.note: Visitors walk up on a paved, very steep trail from the Kuwohi parking area; NPS describes a 1-mile round trip. Seasonal road and tower hours not confirmed.

visit.trail_note: Drive to the Kuwohi parking area, then a steep half-mile paved walk; the ramp lets visitors climb gradually to the platform

events.note: Low bid of $57,000 by W.C. Norris Construction Co., Waynesville, N.C., for an observation tower on Clingmans Dome, reported in a 1958 Kingsport Times item quoted by Forest Lookouts
Concrete observation tower built 1959 under the Mission 66 program (NPS; NC nomination says constructed in 1959)
Marker caption says visitors had climbed a wooden tower before the concrete tower was completed in 1960; ramp wall work shown in 1959
Listed on the National Register of Historic Places 15 August 2012

corrections.proposed: Kuwohi Observation Tower (formerly Clingmans Dome Observation Tower)
corrections.why: The Park Service now calls the tower the Kuwohi Observation Tower and gives Clingmans Dome as its former name

resolved_conflicts.explanation: NPS and the NC nomination give 1959 as the construction year. The marker caption says the concrete tower was completed in 1960 while ramp wall work was in 1959. The story uses 1959 and reports the caption.
NPS calls it an observation tower. The NC nomination says it was intended to function as an auxiliary fire tower, and that the fire cab was dropped. The story reports both.
Tennessee Land Forms lists Sevier County. The NC nomination says the tower straddles the line in Swain County, NC and Sevier County, TN. The story states both.

notes_for_editor: Core construction facts agree across NPS and the NC nomination, except the marker caption's 1960 completion date. The fire-cab history comes from the NC nomination, which is a primary document. Not found: any staffing record or fire it watched. Current road and tower hours were not verified on an NPS page; check before any visit. The Tennessee Land Forms entry is undated. The Clingmans record's name is outdated (see corrections).
